Answer: An employer of a foreign worker must provide private medical insurance throughout the employment period, and must give the worker a summary of the policy in a language the worker understands.

Conditions and exceptions: The insurance usually does not cover a condition that existed before the policy was issued. It will not cover further treatment if an expert medical opinion finds that the worker will not be able to return to work after 90 days of treatment. In that case the worker must return to the country of origin for treatment. If the insurer refuses, the worker can appeal. In many cases the appeal must be filed within 21 days of the refusal notice.

What you can do: Appeal a refusal within the time the handbook describes. The handbook says the worker may ask the assistance organizations listed at the end of the handbook. Their contact details are not repeated here.

Source: PIBA Foreign Workers' Rights Handbook 2026, the handbook section. https://www.gov.il/BlobFolder/policy/bileteral-forms-foreign-workers/he/foreign_workers_rights_booklets_en2026.pdf

claims.quote: Employers of foreign workers are obligated to provide foreign workers with private medical insurance throughout the employment period. The employer must give the employee a summary of the insurance policy in a language the employee understands. The private medical insurance issued to Foreign Workers usually does not cover pre-existing conditions, and will not cover additional medical treatment in cases in which an expert medical opinion finds that the worker will not be able to return to work after 90 days of medical treatment. In such cases, the worker must return to his country of origin for treatment. Therefore, it is very important for the foreign worker to take all steps necessary to retain his rights to medical treatment in his country of origin during his period of work in Israel. If your insurance company refuses to cover certain conditions or treatments, you can appeal this decision. In many cases, this appeal must be filed within 21 days of receiving notice of refusal from the insurance company. You may apply to the NGOs listed at the end of this brochure for assistance in this matter.
